Please audit their account."* #### **4. Consider Reporting to Other Platforms (Optional)** - If you’re really bothered by this, you could also: - **Report to the Better Business Bureau (BBB)** – They track deceptive business practices. - **Post in Amazon Seller Forums** (like r/AmazonSellers on Reddit) – Sometimes collective reports pressure Amazon to act. - **Leave a comment on their other listings** (if you can find them) with a subtle warning (e.g., *"Great product, but beware of their review incentives!"*). ### **Why This Matters:** - **Fake reviews hurt honest sellers** – They manipulate Amazon’s algorithm, making it harder for legitimate small businesses to compete. - **Amazon has tools to detect this** – If enough buyers report the same seller, Amazon’s AI and moderators will likely flag them for review manipulation. - **You’re not the only one** – Many buyers fall for this scam, but reporting (even indirectly) helps protect others. ### **Final Verdict:** **Yes, you’d be justified in reporting them**, but doing so *after* receiving the free item might not be as effective as **strategically leaving a review first** (to make the pattern clearer to Amazon). The best approach is to **combine a slightly suspicious review with a direct report**—this maximizes the chance Amazon will investigate.
